title: K-injective representative of the module derived exchange mate
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and let $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$ form a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], so $fg'=gf'$. Work in the constant-ring module categories $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and their unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Use the exact inverse-image adjunctions $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], with sheaf counits $\varepsilon_u^0$, and the derived functors, derived adjunctions and square comparison specified in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. Write $Q_T$ for localization of complexes on $T$ into $D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$. Let $\theta^0_\square:f'^{-1}g^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}g'^{-1}f^{-1}$ be the module sheaf composition isomorphism whose termwise descent is the square comparison of that definition. Define $\Ex^0_{\square,F}:g^{-1}f_*F\to f'_*g'^{-1}F$ to be the transpose of $g'^{-1}\varepsilon^0_{f,F}\circ\theta^0_{\square,f_*F}$ under the module adjunction, equivalently its unit-square-counit mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate].

For any $K\in D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, choose a K-injective complex $I$, an isomorphism $s:K\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_XI$, and a quasi-isomorphism $j:g'^{-1}I\to J$ with $J$ K-injective [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]. There is no boundedness assumption on $K,I,J$. Naturality of $\Ex^0$ gives a morphism of complexes, and put
$$e=f'_*(j)\circ\Ex^0_{\square,I}:g^{-1}f_*I\longrightarrow f'_*J.$$
Use the canonical K-injective direct-image comparisons of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], that is, the derived-functor comparisons $Q(u_*P)\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_*(QP)$ for K-injective $P$ of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], to define $\chi_{I,s}:Q_Y(f_*I)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*K$ and $\chi_{J,t}:Q_{Y'}(f'_*J)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*g'^{-1}K$, where $\varphi^u_P:u^{-1}Q_TP\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_S(u^{-1}P)$ is the exact termwise comparison for $u:S\to T$ in that definition and $t=Q_{X'}(j)\circ\varphi^{g'}_I\circ g'^{-1}(s)$. Thus $\chi_{I,s}$ is the canonical comparison $Q_Y(f_*I)\cong Rf_*Q_XI$ followed by $Rf_*(s^{-1})$, and $\chi_{J,t}$ is the canonical comparison $Q_{Y'}(f'_*J)\cong Rf'_*Q_{X'}J$ followed by $Rf'_*(t^{-1})$. Set
$$\sigma_{\rm src}=g^{-1}(\chi_{I,s})\circ(\varphi^g_{f_*I})^{-1},\qquad\sigma_{\rm tgt}=\chi_{J,t}.$$
The specified unbounded module exchange mate $\Ex_{\square,K}$ of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] satisfies
$$\Ex_{\square,K}\circ\sigma_{\rm src}=\sigma_{\rm tgt}\circ Q_{Y'}(e).$$
Consequently every such pair of representatives gives the same exchange morphism after these canonical identifications. In particular this applies to bounded below $K$, a bounded below injective resolution $I$ and any K-injective replacement $j$; no preservation of K-injectivity by $g'^{-1}$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0736 (lemma-base-change-map-flat-case), injective-complex construction, and Tag 07A7 (remark-base-change), derived adjoint transpose; comparison for arbitrary module K-injective representatives, with derived.tex Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective), 070K (lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies) and 0DVC (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors). The comparison is an agent-formulated supporting statement, not quoted as a Stacks theorem.

proof.text:
Put $M=g^{-1}f_*I$. The units and counits of the module adjunction have the underlying abelian-sheaf units and counits by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Hence the module mate $\Ex^0$ in the statement is the module-linear natural transformation of [lem-weil-pbc-underived-exchange-module-linear]. Naturality with respect to $d_I^r$ says $d_{f'_*g'^{-1}I}^r\Ex^0_{I^r}=\Ex^0_{I^{r+1}}d_M^r$, so its components are a chain map and $e=f'_*(j)\Ex^0_I$ is a chain map. The termwise adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy], together with naturality of its counit, gives the following equality of chain maps, not just of derived morphisms:
$$\varepsilon^0_{f',J}\,f'^{-1}(e)=j\,\varepsilon^0_{f',g'^{-1}I}\,f'^{-1}(\Ex^0_I)=j\,g'^{-1}(\varepsilon^0_{f,I})\,\theta^0_{\square,f_*I}.$$
The second equality is precisely the defining transpose equation for $\Ex^0$ in each degree. Denote $H=g'^{-1}(\varepsilon^0_{f,I})\theta^0_{\square,f_*I}:f'^{-1}M\to g'^{-1}I$.

source.place: Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives, proof (adjunction on homotopy categories); the chain-level exchange calculation follows sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A7, remark-base-change

proof.text:
Write $\gamma^u_P:Q(u_*P)\to Ru_*(QP)$ for the natural right-derived comparison. The section formula of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] makes $u_*$ additive. For a chain map $a:A\to B$, additivity identifies $u_*(\operatorname{Cone}(a))^r=u_*(B^r\oplus A^{r+1})$ with $(u_*B)^r\oplus(u_*A)^{r+1}$ and carries its differential matrix to the cone differential of $u_*(a)$; it also commutes with shifts. Thus the homotopy functor followed by $Q$ meets the triangulated-exact hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. The existence assertion of [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist] supplies its remaining hypothesis in the module categories; in particular $\gamma^f_I$ and $\gamma^{f'}_J$ are isomorphisms. Exactness in [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] give the natural comparison $\varphi^u_P:u^{-1}QP\cong Q(u^{-1}P)$ used in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. Localization inverts the quasi-isomorphism $j$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Thus $t=Q(j)\varphi^{g'}_I g'^{-1}(s)$ is invertible. Consequently
$$\chi_{I,s}=Rf_*(s^{-1})\gamma^f_I,\qquad \chi_{J,t}=Rf'_*(t^{-1})\gamma^{f'}_J$$
are isomorphisms with exactly the domains and codomains in the statement, as are $\sigma_{\rm src}=g^{-1}(\chi_{I,s})(\varphi^g_{f_*I})^{-1}$ and $\sigma_{\rm tgt}=\chi_{J,t}$.

source.place: Tag 070K, lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies, and Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined (canonical comparison on K-injectives); exact inverse images as in sites-cohomology.tex Section 0735

proof.text:
We compute the canonical derived transpose, rather than assuming a compatibility of counits. Fix an edge $u:U\to V$, a K-injective complex $P$ on $U$, and a complex $N$ on $V$. The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] hold by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], so $u_*P$ is K-injective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] to the two targets $P$ and $u_*P$, and the homotopy adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] between them. With $\varphi$ and $\gamma$ from step 2 this is the canonical derived Hom bijection of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], computed as
$$\Hom_D(u^{-1}QN,QP)\cong\Hom_D(Q(u^{-1}N),QP)\cong\Hom_{K}(u^{-1}N,P)\cong\Hom_{K}(N,u_*P)\cong\Hom_D(QN,Q(u_*P))\cong\Hom_D(QN,Ru_*QP).$$
Here $K$ in the Hom subscripts means the homotopy category, not the fixed derived object of the item. Each arrow is the indicated natural bijection; at a K-injective target this is exactly the localization of the sheaf adjunction, so it computes the specified canonical derived adjunction. In particular, for a chain map $a:N\to u_*P$, the inverse bijection sends $\gamma^u_P Q(a)$ to $Q(\varepsilon^0_{u,P}\,u^{-1}(a))\varphi^u_N$. Taking $N=u_*P$ and $a=1$ gives
$$\varepsilon_{u,QP}\,u^{-1}(\gamma^u_P)=Q(\varepsilon^0_{u,P})\varphi^u_{u_*P}.$$
Naturality of the derived adjunction in an isomorphism $r:L\cong QP$ then shows that the transpose of $Ru_*(r^{-1})\gamma^u_P Q(a)$ is
$$r^{-1}Q(\varepsilon^0_{u,P}\,u^{-1}(a))\varphi^u_N.$$
This calculation works for unbounded complexes: both localization Hom computations require K-injectivity of their targets, with no degree bound.

proof.text:
Let $\rho=\varphi^g_{f_*I}$ and $\beta=\varphi^{f'}_M$. By the mate definition [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], the transpose under $f'^{-1}\dashv Rf'_*$ of $\Ex_{\square,K}\sigma_{\rm src}$ is
$$g'^{-1}(\varepsilon_{f,K})\theta^D_{\square,Rf_*K}\,f'^{-1}(\sigma_{\rm src}).$$
Naturality of $\theta^D$, followed by naturality of $\varepsilon_f$ along $s^{-1}$, rewrites this as
$$g'^{-1}(s^{-1})\,g'^{-1}\bigl(\varepsilon_{f,QI}\,f^{-1}(\gamma^f_I)\bigr)\theta^D_{\square,Q(f_*I)}\,f'^{-1}(\rho^{-1}).$$
Substitute the counit equation proved in step 3. The termwise descent specifying $\theta^D$ in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] gives the explicit compatibility
$$g'^{-1}(\varphi^f_{f_*I})\theta^D_{\square,Q(f_*I)}\,f'^{-1}(\rho^{-1})=(\varphi^{g'}_{f^{-1}f_*I})^{-1}Q(\theta^0_{\square,f_*I})\beta.$$
This is the component formula for descending a natural transformation in clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], with the composite inverse-image comparisons. Finally naturality of $\varphi^{g'}$ for $\varepsilon^0_{f,I}$ moves that counit past the comparison. The transpose is therefore exactly
$$B=g'^{-1}(s^{-1})(\varphi^{g'}_I)^{-1}Q(H)\beta:f'^{-1}(QM)\longrightarrow g'^{-1}K.$$
All composition orders and comparison inverses are displayed here.

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change, in sites-cohomology.tex (adjoint of the inverse-image square followed by the counit); the localization calculation uses the specified termwise descent

proof.text:
Apply the last formula of step 3 to $u=f'$, $P=J$, $N=M$, $r=t$, and $a=e$. The transpose of $\sigma_{\rm tgt}Q(e)=\chi_{J,t}Q(e)$ is
$$t^{-1}Q\bigl(\varepsilon^0_{f',J}f'^{-1}(e)\bigr)\beta=t^{-1}Q(j)Q(H)\beta,$$
where the equality is the chain-map identity in step 1. Expanding the definition of $t$ cancels $Q(j)$ and gives
$$t^{-1}Q(j)Q(H)\beta=g'^{-1}(s^{-1})(\varphi^{g'}_I)^{-1}Q(H)\beta=B.$$
Thus the two morphisms in question have the same transpose. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection, equivalently the mate-transpose characterization of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], now gives
$$\Ex_{\square,K}\sigma_{\rm src}=\sigma_{\rm tgt}Q(e).$$

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change, in sites-cohomology.tex; substitution of the two explicit transpose calculations of steps 1, 3 and 4

proof.text: Since both comparison maps in step 2 are invertible, the equation gives $\sigma_{\rm tgt}Q(e)\sigma_{\rm src}^{-1}=\Ex_{\square,K}$. The proof used only the stated properties of $(I,s,j)$, so every such triple gives this same fixed mate after its own canonical identifications. A bounded below complex of injective modules is K-injective by [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; hence the stated bounded below example is included. At no point was $g'^{-1}I$ asserted K-injective: the target used in the transpose computation is the separately chosen $J$.
